items.entity: FEM-TO design domain (vertical extent / designable height)
items.description: Nanopillar Results paragraph gives the domain as 162.00 x 162.00 x 413.10 Å (= 40 x 40 x 102 FCC cells), but this box includes the 12,800 passive 'clamped base' atoms. The base thickness is never stated (atom counts imply 2 cells = 8.10 Å). Supplementary Note A.14 (not provided) does not say whether the FEM domain is the full box with a non-design base layer or only the ~405 Å active region.
readings: Full 162 x 162 x 413.10 Å box; bottom 8.10 Å is non-design solid, so the designable region is 162 x 162 x 405.00 Å
Full 162 x 162 x 413.10 Å box, all designable (base represented only by boundary conditions)
Only the active region 162 x 162 x 405.00 Å is modeled; base omitted

items.description: Results gives only a count ('12,800 are passive atoms from the clamped base'). Methods says passive atoms stay real and represent the anchored base. Shape and thickness are not stated. 12,800 = 4 x 40 x 40 x 2 suggests a full-footprint slab 2 unit cells thick. The 11.25% surface fraction of the initial column also matches an 18x18x100-cell column whose bottom sits on that slab. But because the pillar is 'supported at the four corners', an engineer could instead model corner blocks, or leave out passive solid in the FEM model.
readings: Full-footprint non-design solid slab 162 x 162 x 8.10 Å at z = 0 to 8.10 Å
Four non-design corner blocks with the same total volume (e.g., 40.5 x 40.5 x 32.4 Å each = 10x10x8 cells)
No passive solid region in the FEM model (supports applied directly to design-domain nodes)

items.description: Results says 'The pillar is supported at the four corners of the base' and mentions 'four corner supports'; the Discussion says load is 'redirected into the four supports'. But the same Results paragraph calls the passive atoms 'the clamped base', and Methods says passive atoms are 'held fixed in all Cartesian directions', which would clamp the whole base. No size is given for the corner supports. The corner 'roots' and the 3.65x stiffness gain over a central column fit discrete corner supports.
readings: Whole base / entire bottom face clamped (all 12,800 passive atoms fixed)
Single nodes at the four bottom corners (point supports)
Four square bottom-corner patches 4.05 x 4.05 Å (1 cell, 0.025 of side)
Four square bottom-corner patches 20.25 x 20.25 Å (5 cells, 0.125 of side)
Four square bottom-corner patches 40.5 x 40.5 Å (10 cells, 0.25 of side)
Nodes along the four vertical corner edges of the 8.10 Å base slab

items.description: 'Supported at the four corners' does not say which displacement components are held. Methods' 'held fixed in all Cartesian directions' applies to passive atoms. If only the corner regions are supported, the FEM-TO (Note A.14, unavailable) could use either full fixity or vertical-only supports. That decides whether the supports can carry the horizontal thrust from splayed corner legs.
readings: u_x = u_y = u_z = 0 at support nodes (clamped/pinned)
u_z = 0 only at the corners, plus minimal in-plane restraints against rigid-body motion (rollers)

items.entity: vertical load at center of top surface
items.description: Results/Methods say only that a vertical displacement of 1% of the height is applied 'at the center of the top surface' (Fig. 6a red arrow; the text also mentions a 'top contact'). Not stated: the number of loaded atoms or the patch size; whether the loaded atoms are held laterally; or how the displacement becomes a load in a force-driven minimum-compliance FEM-TO. For a patch, a uniform prescribed displacement and a uniform traction give different optima.
readings: Concentrated vertical force at the single top-center node
Uniform vertical force over a centered 4.05 x 4.05 Å (1 cell) or 8.10 x 8.10 Å (2x2 cells) patch
Uniform prescribed vertical displacement (rigid punch) on such a patch, lateral DOFs free
Rigid punch on such a patch with lateral DOFs also fixed
Load spread over the whole 72.9 x 72.9 Å top face of the initial column (0.45 of side)

items.description: Methods: delta_pillar = 1% of 'the pillar height'. This could mean the 413.10 Å domain height or the ~405 Å active height. Note A.14 gives no force magnitude for the force-based FEM-TO.
readings: Prescribed displacement 4.131 Å (1% of 413.10 Å)
Prescribed displacement 4.05 Å (1% of 405.00 Å)
Unit force F = 1 (force-controlled FEM-TO)

items.description: Results: target mass ratio 20.25%, and FEM-TO solved 'the same nanopillar problem'. 'Mass ratio' is never defined. The numbers imply it is relative to active atoms only (cantilever: 88,500/148,500 = 59.60%; pillar: 129,600/640,000 = 0.2025 = 0.45^2). Still, a FEM code with passive base elements may count those elements in the volume.
readings: 0.2025 of the designable (active) region only (129,600 of 640,000 active atoms)
0.2025 of the whole domain including the passive base (about 0.1866 of the designable region)

items.description: Only 'aluminum' (Mishin EAM potential, a0 = 4.05 Å) is given. No continuum modulus is stated for the FEM-TO in Note A.14.
readings: E = 70 GPa (handbook aluminum)
E = 1 (normalized)
Isotropic modulus averaged from the Mishin-EAM cubic elastic constants

items.entity: Poisson's ratio / elastic symmetry for FEM-TO
items.description: Poisson's ratio is not given. The text calls Al 'nearly isotropic' but does not say whether FEM-TO used isotropic or cubic elasticity (Methods: cube edges aligned with x, y, z).
readings: Isotropic, nu = 0.33
Isotropic, nu = 0.3
Cubic anisotropic Al stiffness with cube axes along x, y, z

items.description: Results says only that the FEM-TO layout is 'mapped onto the same FCC lattice' (Note A.14, Figs. S17-S18 unavailable). Element type, element size and grid dimensions are not given.
readings: 40 x 40 x 102 (or 40 x 40 x 100 without base) cubic 8-node hex elements of 4.05 Å, one per FCC unit cell
80 x 80 x 204 (or 80 x 80 x 200) cubic elements of 2.025 Å, one per atomic-plane voxel
20 x 20 x 51 cubic elements of 8.10 Å

items.description: The only filter described is the Nano-TO multi-shell atomistic sensitivity filter (Methods: r_min = 10.325 Å 'unless otherwise noted'). The FEM-TO filter type and radius are not given.
readings: Density filter, r_min = 10.325 Å (about 2.55 elements at 4.05 Å; about 5.1 elements at 2.025 Å)
Sensitivity filter, r_min = 1.5 elements
Density filter, r_min = 3 elements

items.description: The comparison is described only as 'FEM-based TO'. SIMP penalty, void stiffness, continuation and projection are not given.
readings: SIMP p = 3, E_min = 1e-9 E, no projection
SIMP with penalty continuation p = 1 to 3
SIMP p = 3 plus Heaviside projection with beta continuation

items.description: No update scheme or convergence criterion is given for FEM-TO. The period-two-cycle and 3,000-iteration rules in Methods apply to Nano-TO only.
readings: Optimality criteria, move limit 0.2, stop when max density change < 0.01
MMA with a fixed iteration budget (e.g., 200-300 iterations)

items.description: Results: Nano-TO starts from 'a uniform prismatic column at that mass ratio'. The column's size and position are not stated (0.45^2 implies a centered 72.9 Å, 18x18-cell square column). It is also not said whether FEM-TO started from this column or from a uniform density field.
readings: Uniform density 0.2025 over the design region
Centered 72.9 x 72.9 Å solid square prismatic column through the design height, void elsewhere

items.description: Mirror symmetry is stated only for the cantilevers. Nothing is said about symmetry for the pillar or its FEM-TO, although loads and supports are square-symmetric.
readings: No symmetry imposed (full model)
Mirror planes x = 81 Å and y = 81 Å (quarter model)
Full square symmetry including diagonal mirrors (1/8 model)

items.entity: conversion of FEM-TO densities to FCC atoms (design in Fig. S18)
items.description: Results says only that the FEM-TO layout 'is mapped onto the same FCC lattice'. The threshold rule, and whether the mapped design is trimmed to exactly 20.25%, are not stated. These decide the final binary design that is evaluated (3.44 normalized stiffness).
readings: Threshold element density at 0.5; each atom inherits the density of its containing element
Rank-order threshold keeping exactly 129,600 active atoms (20.25%)
Threshold on nodal densities interpolated at atom positions

locator: Supplementary Note A.14, the nanopillar designed by FEM-TO (Fig. S18)
